summary: Built the canonical revit-bridge v2 IFC exporter (skills/revit-bridge/assets/ifc-export.js) as a dependency-free ES module drop-in for Design's <three-d-stage> (`toIfc(THREE, object, meta)` unchanged; adds `exportIfc()→{text,report}`), implementing every R1–R10 requirement: real per-product IfcLocalPlacements decomposed from world matrices with a consistent y-up→z-up mapping; parametric IfcExtrudedAreaSolids for un-baked Box (rectangle), Cylinder rt==rb (circle) and ExtrudeGeometry shapes-with-holes (IfcArbitraryProfileDefWithVoids via a shared IfcCartesianPointList2D + IfcIndexedPolyCurve rings) with a bbox-vs-parameters check that sends baked/merged geometry to the IfcTriangulatedFaceSet fallback (meta.geometry auto|tessellation|solids); shared IfcXxxTypes deduped by (ifcClass,typeName) with one IfcRelDefinesByType; two-level instancing (mesh-level maps by geometry content+material, plus assembly-level maps for identical whole products, attached to the shared type's RepresentationMaps and a shared IfcProductDefinitionShape); exclusions (ifc:false/ifcExclude/helper/excludeNames with clearanceAs skip|space|proxy); multi-storey structure with per-storey containment and IFCSPACE aggregation + elevation inference; minFeatureSize + ifcLOD skip|bbox|full; author/site/building/IfcApplication 'revit-bridge exporter'; seeded deterministic GUIDs, ISO-10303-21 \X2\ escaping, and an entity-count report. Wrote the demo assembly (example-model.js) exercising every feature and a Node+Python harness that exports both modes and validates with ifcopenshell 0.8.5 — all assertions pass.
key_findings: Both example exports (auto and tessellation) are IFC4, parse with ifcopenshell 0.8.5 and report ZERO issues under ifcopenshell.validate json rules; the auto file also passes the strict EXPRESS WHERE rules except one known false positive: the official IFC4 schema misspells IFCTRANFORMERTYPE in IfcTransformer.CorrectTypeAssigned (missing 's'), so any correctly-typed IfcTransformer trips it — a schema defect to whitelist in validate_ifc.py, not an export bug.

Geometric correctness of R1/R2 was validated numerically: per-product world bounding boxes computed by ifcopenshell.geom from the solid (auto) export match the independent tessellated export to 0.2 mm across all 7 products, including a panel rotated 90 degrees (insertion point (3.32,-0.6,1.0), local x → world −y), proving the placement decomposition (Axis=convert(node +Y), RefDirection=convert(node +X)) and the Box/Cylinder/Extrude solid frames are consistent with the y-up→z-up mapping (x,y,z)→(x,−z,y).

Instancing shrinks BYTES ~9x (43.8 KB auto vs 389.7 KB tessellation) but entity COUNT only via assembly-level sharing: mesh-level IfcMappedItem instancing costs ~3 entities per occurrence — the same as a tessellated mesh — so the exporter also dedupes identical whole PRODUCTS onto one IfcRepresentationMap (attached to the shared IfcXxxType.RepresentationMaps) with a shared IfcProductDefinitionShape (legal in IFC4, ShapeOfProduct is a SET), plus one shared point list per holed profile; result 593 entities auto vs 629 tessellation. SKILL/report copy should quote byte reduction, not entity counts.

R3 verified: the two identical ground-floor panelboards produce exactly ONE IfcElectricDistributionBoardType (with the typePsets attached once and the type-level RepresentationMap referenced by both occurrences' IfcMappedItems), a single IfcRelDefinesByType lists both, and the differently-named Level-2 board gets its own type; v1's per-element type duplication is fixed.

R5/R6/R7 verified: working_clearance (helper) and door_swing_clearance nodes and ifcLOD='skip' screws never appear as products or geometry (clearanceAs:'space' turns them into IfcSpaces instead); IFCSPACE nodes are aggregated to their storey via IfcRelAggregates (not contained); storeys Level 1@0/Level 2@4 with one IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure each; storey chosen by userData.ifc.storey (name/index) or inferred from world elevation.

R9 verified: with meta.guidSeed the export is byte-identical across re-export and across a full model rebuild (GUIDs derived per-entity from a stable node/type key, so unrelated edits don't shift other GlobalIds); string escaping round-trips em-dash/Ø/″ via \X2\....\X0\ and apostrophes via doubling; zero dangling # references. Backward-compat: an untagged object becomes one product from meta (v1 rule), tessellation mode emits only IfcTriangulatedFaceSet with instancing off by default, and meta.placements:'world' reproduces v1 identity placements exactly.

open_questions: Revit import empirics are unverified: does Revit's Open/Link IFC honour (a) products sharing one IfcProductDefinitionShape (schema-legal in IFC4), (b) nested IfcMappedItems (breaker maps inside the panel assembly map), and (c) IfcIndexedPolyCurve profile rings (fine for Revit ≥2016)? If the brothers' Revit is old, an IfcPolyline fallback for profiles and un-shared PDS may be needed — one flag away.

Products whose whole body is instanced (identical panels) currently share their assembly IfcRepresentationMap even when their types differ; the map is only ATTACHED to a type when the assembly group exactly equals that type's occurrence set. Should mixed-type identical bodies be forced apart? Current behaviour is valid but worth a policy decision.

The exporter reports 'entity count' per R10, but instancing's real payoff is bytes (≈9x), not entities (mesh-level IfcMappedItem ≈ 3 entities per occurrence, same as a faceset). Recommend SKILL.md/report.py cite byte reduction; the 'auto entities < tessellation entities' property holds for this example via assembly-level sharing but is not guaranteed for arbitrary models.
